correctness.rationale: For each vertex v in part V_i, the neighborhood sum is w-s_i+f(v), so checking the minimum label in each part is necessary and sufficient. The local Laurent-polynomial cases are disjoint and exhaustive, and coefficient extraction enforces the global weight. Exhaustive independent replay through order 9 agrees with the literal definition and all coefficients.

originality.rationale: The closest primary source, arXiv:1205.0343v1, determines scalar signed, signed-total, and minus domination numbers of complete multipartite graphs. Its Theorem 3 states the scalar minus domination number and does not state a weight-distribution enumerator. The earlier biclique paper is also scalar. Searches of published semantic-index findings and web literature found no exact all-function enumerator; residual terminology/indexing risk remains.
residual_risks: An older or poorly indexed paper may count minus dominating functions under nonstandard terminology such as a generating function or feasible-labeling census.
The term minus domination polynomial is not standardized; the retained claim therefore defines its weight enumerator explicitly rather than asserting terminology priority.

value.rationale: The theorem upgrades a classical scalar invariant on a natural graph class to a complete structural and coefficient-level census. It answers the number of feasible labelings at every weight and is directly reusable for counting or probabilistic questions; it is not a renaming of the known minimum formula.
